hook: David Lowe began his academic career as an Assistant Professor at New York University's Courant Institute before joining the University of British Columbia's Computer Science Department in 1987, where he became a full professor and remained for nearly three decades. In 1999 he introduced the Scale-Invariant Feature Transform, known as SIFT, a method for extracting distinctive local features from images that remain recognizable across changes in scale, rotation, and lighting. His fully developed 2004 paper on the method became one of the most cited papers in computer vision history, and SIFT became a standard tool for tasks ranging from panorama stitching to robot navigation and object recognition. In 2009 Lowe co-founded Cloudburst Research, a computer vision startup that was acquired by Google in 2015, after which he worked as a Senior Research Scientist within Google's Machine Intelligence group. He has since returned to UBC as Professor Emeritus.

They also record the 1999 introduction and 2004 full publication of SIFT, the founding of Cloudburst Research in 2009, and that startup's acquisition by Google in 2015. Taken together, the records show a computer vision researcher whose method became a standard tool, whose startup was acquired by Google, and whose recent coverage sits within debates about AI safety and whistleblowing.
standing.standing: David Lowe is Professor Emeritus of Computer Science at the University of British Columbia, according to the records. He introduced the Scale-Invariant Feature Transform, first presented in 1999 and published in full in 2004. That method became one of the most cited papers in computer vision history and a standard tool for tasks such as panorama stitching, robot navigation, and object recognition. He co-founded Cloudburst Research, which Google acquired in 2015, and he then worked as a Senior Research Scientist in Google's Machine Intelligence group from 2015 to 2018. His record includes the Helmholtz Prize at ICCV in 2011 and 2017 and the IEEE PAMI Distinguished Researcher Award in 2015.

timeline.event: Became an Assistant Professor of Computer Science at NYU's Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences.
timeline.impact: Began his academic research career in computer vision.

timeline.event: Joined the University of British Columbia as a Professor of Computer Science.
timeline.impact: Established what became a leading computer vision research program in Canada.

timeline.event: First presented the Scale-Invariant Feature Transform (SIFT) method.
timeline.impact: Introduced a new approach to detecting stable, distinctive features in images.

timeline.event: Published the definitive SIFT paper, 'Distinctive Image Features from Scale-Invariant Keypoints,' in the International Journal of Computer Vision.
timeline.impact: Became one of the most cited papers in computer vision, with SIFT adopted across image matching, robotics, and augmented reality applications.

timeline.event: Co-founded Cloudburst Research, a computer vision startup.
timeline.impact: Applied his research commercially to real time mobile computer vision applications.

timeline.event: Received the Helmholtz Prize at ICCV for the SIFT paper's lasting impact.
timeline.impact: Recognized as one of the most influential papers in the field a decade after publication.

timeline.event: Cloudburst Research was acquired by Google, and Lowe joined Google's Machine Intelligence group as a Senior Research Scientist.
timeline.impact: Brought his feature detection research into Google's computer vision and machine learning products.

timeline.event: Received a second Helmholtz Prize at ICCV.
timeline.impact: Reaffirmed the enduring influence of his work on invariant feature detection.
